source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 【During Test】 - 2GB or more of system memory - Linux kernel 2.6.16 or later Kernel 2.6.29 or later is recommended for performance reasons. The tool has been tested with kernels 2.6.16 through 2.6.35. - glibc 2.12 or later required by Python3.10 - 64-bit x86_64 kernels are supported. 32-bit kernels are not supported. - TinyLinux version 12.08 or later is supported. - Configured to run one of the following supported OSs: • Ubuntu 22.04 w/ NVIDIA optimized kernel v6.2 • RHEL 9.2 z-stream with kernel v5.14 • SLES 15 SP5 Security Update (SU) with kernel v5.14 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: When completed, the diagnostic will return 0 to the shell if completed normally. If an error occurs, it will return 1 to the shell, and if a retest is required it will return 2. It will also print “PASS”, “FAIL”, or “RETEST” to the screen. PASS – The hardware passes the diagnostics FAIL – The hardware has failed the diagnostics RETEST – The hardware setup has failed the pre-check portion of the diagnostics and a warning message appears describing the problem. Correct the problem per the pre-check message and then test again.

test_case.test_name: Field RMA Diagnostics — parameterized review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Run the authorized NVIDIA field-RMA diagnostic once on a supported SUT and classify its complete result strictly as PASS, FAIL or RETEST using both process status and tool markers.
required_package: Diagnostic package name/version/hash/license and authoritative runbook
Exact executable, arguments, privileges, working directory, timeout and output locations
Monitoring/abort/recovery plus PASS/FAIL/RETEST and inconsistent-result disposition
test_case.test_command: Verify package hash/license/signature, supported OS/kernel/glibc/Python/driver/firmware/topology and official runbook; capture baseline health; execute the approved diagnostic and arguments once under monitoring; preserve complete stdout/stderr, exit status and artifacts; reconcile exit 0/1/2 with PASS/FAIL/RETEST text.
test_case.expected_result: The diagnostic completes within the approved timeout and returns a consistent 0+PASS, 1+FAIL or 2+RETEST result with complete artifacts and no safety abort.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS is only consistent exit 0 and PASS with complete coverage. Exit 1/FAIL is FAIL. Exit 2/RETEST, marker/status inconsistency, unsupported platform, incomplete output or health abort is not PASS and requires engineer disposition; no automatic rerun is allowed.
safety_gate: Use only verified authorized package on supported isolated SUT
Preserve full output/exit code and monitor GPU/host/BMC health
Stop on timeout/crash/health anomaly or unsupported pre-check
Do not auto-install/fix/retest, truncate evidence or convert tool PASS/FAIL into DUT verdict
expected_evidence: Full stdout/stderr, output artifacts, timestamps and shell exit code
Final PASS/FAIL/RETEST marker plus pre-check/error reason and consistency check
GPU/host/BMC health, engineer disposition and verdict
test_case.recovery: Stop on package, compatibility or health failure, preserve artifacts and restore temporary services/settings per the vendor runbook. Any RETEST correction and rerun needs a new explicit authorization.
